subject: VPC subnet ownership and data traceability — evidence request
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@medisys.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisys.com
Date: 2028-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency + VPC topology ask for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of MediSys' SIG/CAIQ intake and our internal compliance review, Security has asked for a short packet covering how Redwood maps customer tenant data to hosting regions and which private-network constructs are used for MediSys workloads. Specifically we need:

- A VPC/subnet ownership map that indicates which subnets host MediSys compute + storage (region, AZ, CIDR), and whether those subnets are dedicated or multi-tenant.
- Operator roster: who (by role) has console/SSH access to the private deployment, including a point-of-contact for on-call escalations.
- Egress controls: sample firewall/egress-filter rules and how we prevent cross-region data leakage.
- Evidence that tenant-to-region mapping is enforced (config snippet, flow logs, or short runbook steps).
- Reference pointers to SOC 2 / CAIQ control IDs that cover network segregation and key management.

Can you provide the packet plus any attestation letter that an authorized Redwood representative can sign? Ideally we need this by COB next Wednesday (2028-04-03) to keep our internal intake on schedule.

If anything here is sensitive, flag it and we can take it into a secure portal.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Wu
Security Program Manager, MediSys Health
alice.wu@medisys.com
Phone: +1 (617) 555-0148

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for. Quick plan and owners:

- VPC/subnet map and sample topology PDF (owner: Network Ops — Irene Choi).
- Operator roster CSV (owner: Security Ops — Grace O'Connor).
- Sample egress-filter rules and short explanation of how they are applied across privatelink endpoints (owner: Network Ops).
- Tenant mapping evidence: we'll include a short flow-log excerpt + a config extract from the routing policy that enforces region pinning.
- Control references: we'll annotate CAIQ/SIG IDs (CCM items) and point to the SOC 2 section in our compliance folder.

Attachments: I'll start with a preliminary topology snapshot and example rules; final packet will include a signed attestation letter from our Head of Trust.

Proposal: 30-min sync tomorrow 2028-03-27 11:00am ET to walk the artifacts; if that works I can send calendar invite.

Deliverable ETA: draft packet by 2028-03-29, final signed packet by 2028-04-02.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Hi Alice — forwarding the initial network snapshot (see attachment stub: privatelink_subnet_map_v1.pdf). A few technical clarifications to set expectations: 

- Dedicated vs shared: MediSys pilot is deployed in dedicated subnets (us-east-1a/us-east-1b) behind private endpoints. We will call out any non-dedicated control plane components in the packet.
- Egress controls: we enforce egress filtering at the privatelink gateway and again at host-level iptables for infrequent secondary enforcement. Attached is a sample of the egress-filter rules we apply (egress-filter-sample-rules.txt).
- Tenant-to-region mapping: our routing policy attaches tenant IDs to a region tag on pod metadata; enforcement is evaluated during allocation. We'll include a sanitized routing-config snippet and a 72-hour flow-log extract showing accepted flows staying within us-east-1.

Forwarded message follows for context:

Tessa / Irene —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups before we ingest the packet into our CAIQ workspace:

- Operator roster: can you provide the CSV with roles (name, role, access type, justification, last training date) rather than the consolidated internal list? We need the justification column for our audit. (Attachment name request: operator-roster.csv)
- Signed attestation: do you have a one-page attestation stating that MediSys workloads are pinned to US regions and that operator access is limited to the roster provided? If possible include signatory name, title, and date.
- Evidence sensitivity: the flow-log extract is fine, but please redact IPs outside of MediSys ranges.

If you can deliver those three items by Tuesday 2028-04-02 morning ET we can complete our CAIQ mapping and send back any clarifying questions.

Thanks —
Alice

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@medisys.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-02T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Final packet: operator roster, egress rules, attestation and short runbook

Hi Alice —

Attached: operator-roster.csv (CSV), egress-filter-sample-rules.txt, privatelink_subnet_map_v1.pdf. Also included is a one-page attestation signed by our Head of Trust (digital signature stub referenced). Highlights below: 

- Tenant residency: MediSys tenant IDs are pinned to us-east-1a/us-east-1b via the allocation service; enforcement is validated via automated allocation checks (see control check ID: CAIQ-NET-3a in the packet).
- Keystore & KMS: tenant keys are maintained in a regional KMS instance with separate key aliases per-tenant; operator roles do not have access to raw key material (see SOC2 control reference: CC6.5).
- Operator access: CSV includes name, role, access type (console/ssh/ops-api), justification, and last training date. Access is provisioned via RBAC group and reviewed quarterly.
- Egress filtering: ruleset is applied at privatelink gateway and host; example rules redact external IP ranges and show deny-by-default posture.
- Traceability runbook (short): steps to verify region pinning using flow logs + allocation API (included as plaintext). We also include a sample traceroute output with timestamps (sanitized).

Next steps we recommend: 1) MediSys security to review packet and raise clarifying questions on SEC-445 in our Jira board, 2) If you need a signed paper letter (wet signature), we can produce that via your vendor intake form.

If you'd like a 20-min walkthrough of the attachments, I'm available tomorrow 2028-04-03 10:00am ET.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
